newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto defends his economic, political policies.
newsitem.headline: Suharto defends his economic, political policies.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto defended his economic and political policies on Thursday, saying national stability was needed for development.
"Only with national stability can we develop," Suharto told a gathering of businessmen in Bogor, some 60 km (37 miles) south of Jakarta.
"There is no country that can develop without a guarantee of national stability in the field of politics, economy, society, culture and security," he said.
Suharto said there had been criticism that Indonesia's emphasis on national stability had hampered democracy.
Critics had also said the country's growth model only produced conglomerates, which dominated the economy, he added.
"This is not true. This is only a phase. We are progressing to the next phase," Suharto said.

"Our economic development is not only for growth but it is also for equitability," he said. "The backbone of our national economy is not decided by big business only, it must be supported by small- and medium-scale businesses."
Indonesia has experienced three decades of strong economic growth under Suharto's firm rule.
But the growing economic clout and accumulation of wealth by the conglomerates, many of which are controlled by ethnic-Chinese businessmen, has fuelled resentment across the multi-ethnic country.
Indonesia also holds general elections on May 29. Campaigning has been tightly regulated and the ruling Golkar Party is expected to win easily.
